title: LinkedIn and career workshop
lead: One hour, screen shared, spent on the two things that decide whether you get hired: how you describe yourself, and who sees it.
outcomes: A positioning line that says what you do without sounding like a job advert
Your headline, about section and featured links rewritten while we talk
A 90-day plan: what to post, who to message, and what to say to them

process.title: Book
process.body: Pick a slot and pay. Two minutes, and the card is the only filter.

process.title: I do the homework
process.body: Before we speak I read your profile, your CV, and real job posts for the role you want.

process.title: We work
process.body: Sixty minutes on Google Meet, rewriting in real time rather than talking about rewriting.

process.title: You ship
process.body: You leave with the doc we wrote together and a checklist for the first 30 days.

forYou: You are a few years into your career and the next step is not obvious from where you are standing
You want to move from a big company into a startup, or from doing the work into running it
You have a LinkedIn profile and never post, or you post and nothing happens
You would rather send ten precise messages than two hundred applications
You will do the homework between booking and the call
notForYouLabel: This is not for you if
notForYou: You want someone to apply to jobs on your behalf
You want a guaranteed offer. Nobody can promise that and I will not pretend to
You are a company looking to hire. That is RallyUp, one click away in the nav
You have not decided you are going to change something yet

faq.a: $100, paid when you book. One hour, on Google Meet.
LinkedIn is where the work ends up, not what the work is. We spend most of the hour on how you describe yourself and who you should be talking to.

faq.q: Will you write my posts for me?
faq.a: No. I ghostwrite for executives through RallyUp and that is a different service at a different price. You leave this session able to write your own.

faq.q: What do I need to bring?
faq.a: Your CV, your LinkedIn, and a rough idea of the role you want next. If you only have two of the three, book anyway.
